Incident leadership

Direct the incident from one current picture.

The command view

See what needs attention.

A useful command dashboard puts changing conditions next to the plan they affect. Each signal leads back to its source record.

01 / PRIORITIES

Objectives and direction

Keep the current operational objectives in view while teams carry out their assignments.

02 / RESOURCES

Teams and tasks

See availability, work in progress, and assignments that need a supervisor’s attention.

03 / CONDITIONS

Alerts and safety

Bring hazards, weather changes, and emerging intelligence into command review.

Decision support

Questions command can answer quickly.

The value of the view is in the links between information, action, and accountability.

What changed?Follow new field reports, status transitions, alerts, and intelligence.
Who owns the next action?Trace a need to its task, assigned team, and supervisor.
What is at risk?Compare the plan with safety conditions, weather, and resource readiness.
What must be carried forward?Keep command activity and decisions with the incident record.
Organization

Keep the structure visible.

The organizational view shows how sections, branches, divisions, and groups relate to command. It gives every assignment a clear supervisory path.

  • See who is responsible for each part of the operation.
  • Connect group work to section priorities and incident objectives.
  • Carry the structure into briefings and documentation.
